snapshots.label: September 2026
snapshots.source: Seller listings checked on 17 September 2026 at US tape sellers, published as the September 2026 edition of the LTO price tracker.
snapshots.summary: The September 2026 edition of the LTO price tracker: 165 new listings from 7 US tape sellers, with single-cartridge price ranges and new drive prices for LTO-6 to LTO-10.
snapshots.drivesNote: Seller listings for new standalone SAS drives.
notes: Single new cartridges and new standalone drives from 165 listings at 7 US sellers (BackupWorks, DatacenterDisk, LTO World, MagStor, StoragePartsDirect, Tape4Backup, TapeandMedia), checked on 17 September 2026.
The 40 TB LTO-10 cartridge was listed at $491.00-$555.00 ($12.28-$13.88 per TB); the LTO-10 row above is the 30 TB cartridge.

Tape4Backup shows a site-wide banner: 'From September 1st, 2026, all LTO Tape prices have increased.' Despite that, its LTO-9 singles ($93.50-$99.50) and LTO-10 30TB singles ($256-$286.75) sit in line with other sellers.

Trend vs early 2026: LTO-9 cartridges flat (Symply quoted about $94 in Feb 2026; now $92-$112). LTO-10 30TB roughly flat to slightly down (Symply ~$280 in Feb 2026; now $256-$300). LTO-10 40TB lower than expected launch price (Symply expected ~$570 or $14.25/TB; now $491-$555 or $12.28-$13.88/TB). Symply blamed the 40TB premium on launch pricing, tight Aramid base film supply and hyperscaler deals.

DatacenterDisk (published 2026-08-17, data updated 2026-09-17): LTO tape 'largely stable at $4-$6/TB' while HDD prices rose sharply in 2026; tape's $/TB edge over HDD widened from about 2x to 3.5x. The stated reason is an independent supply chain (Fujifilm and Sony in Japan) that avoids the NAND shortage and hyperscale HDD demand.

LTO Program (Sept 2026): 160.3 EB of LTO capacity shipped in 2025 (down 9% from the 176.5 EB record in 2024); Q1 2026 shipped capacity up 57% YoY, driven by LTO-9 adoption and the LTO-10 ramp; 2026 expected to set a new record.

The Register (2026-09-02): only Sony and Fujifilm make LTO cartridges. Analyst Tom Coughlin tied the 2025 dip to 'the evolving international trade environment' making buyers more cautious (tariff-related caution, but no price figure given).
Blocks & Files (2026-09-04): suggests the 2025 dip may reflect buyers waiting for LTO-10; projects 2026 could reach about 251.67 EB if Q1 pace holds.

Fujifilm LTO Ultrium 10 40TB cartridge (16978170) uses an aramid base film and began shipping January 2026; it works in existing LTO-10 drives. IBM 40TB cartridges (models 564/664) available 2026-03-06.
Half-height LTO-10 drives: Symply support article said HH drives expected Q2 2026 (FH first because of the new head guide assembly). No HH LTO-10 drive was listed at any seller checked on 2026-09-17.

snapshots.label: August 2026
snapshots.source: Generation guide ranges published on TapeBackup.org on 30 August 2026, before the September 2026 refresh.
snapshots.summary: Broad guide ranges used on the LTO-6 to LTO-10 price pages through the summer of 2026. These were rounded planning ranges rather than individual listings, so they are wider than the manufacturer snapshots from 2025.
notes: Drive price tables from this edition were not preserved in a usable form, so only cartridge ranges are archived here.

snapshots.label: March 2026
snapshots.source: TapeBackup.org LTO price summary and drive price guide, first published 16 March 2026.
snapshots.summary: LTO-8 and LTO-9 were the price to capacity sweet spots. LTO-10 drives and media carried an early adopter premium, while LTO-5 and LTO-6 drives were mostly refurbished.
notes: Dell spare part list prices were far above street; third party and refurbished drives sold for $1,800-$2,500.
External drives cost $800-$1,500 more than internal bare drives. Thunderbolt LTO-9 units listed around $6,299.

snapshots.label: January 2026
snapshots.period: January 2026 edition (data from November to December 2025)
snapshots.source: TapeBackup.org January 2026 market analysis, based on November to December 2025 listings.
snapshots.summary: Prices were stable for LTO-5 through LTO-9. LTO-10 media was softening as HPE and IBM priced below the launch Fujifilm listing.
notes: The original edition quoted cost per TB against compressed capacity. Native cost per TB is shown in the table on this page.

snapshots.label: November to December 2025
snapshots.source: TapeBackup.org price tracker, November to December 2025 listings.
snapshots.summary: LTO-8 kept the best cost per TB. LTO-10 media began to soften as IBM and HPE entered below the initial Fujifilm price, LTO-9 held steady with bulk discounts, and supply of LTO-5 to LTO-7 kept thinning.
notes: Barcode labels for library automation added $2-$5 per cartridge.
5, 10 and 20 packs saved roughly 5-15% per cartridge.

snapshots.label: September to October 2025
snapshots.source: TapeBackup.org price tracker, September to October 2025 vendor and manufacturer listings.
snapshots.summary: LTO-8 offered the best cost per TB. LTO-10 30 TB media had only just shipped and was essentially a single Fujifilm listing near $295.
